title: Density of Gaussian torus Fourier functions
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $p$ be a finite real exponent with $1\le p$. Map $x\in\mathbb R^n$ to the torus with coordinates indexed by pairs $(j,\varepsilon)\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, using the circle class of $x_j$ when $\varepsilon=\mathrm{false}$ and of $\sqrt2\,x_j$ when $\varepsilon=\mathrm{true}$. The complex linear span of the pullbacks, under this map, of all torus Fourier characters is dense in $L^p(\mu;\mathbb C)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$
